headline: High: CrewAI’s default write/network/browser capabilities can feed next-ai-draw-io’s MCP/API pipeline, creating prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers, while next-ai-draw-io accepts natural-language commands and uses MCP/API-backed AI flows. A shared file or browser-mediated handoff can let attacker-controlled content from A be treated as instructions by B. The interaction is inferred from documented surfaces, not directly reproduced.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes untrusted content into a workspace file that next-ai-draw-io later ingests
IF next-ai-draw-io parses file content or MCP output as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable automatic ingestion of files from CrewAI outputs
Add provenance tags to all handoffs
Require a human review step before B executes instructions
requires-engineering: enforce content-type and source validation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, and next-ai-draw-io processes PDFs, text, images, and diagrams while calling multiple third-party model APIs. If both touch the same workspace, sensitive inputs from A can be forwarded by B to external inference providers. This is a plausible default-path leakage risk, though not directly evidenced for this pair.
conditions: IF both agents share a filesystem or document workspace
IF B uploads files originating from A to a remote model provider
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Redact secrets before B processes any A-generated files
Restrict B to local-only models
Turn off automatic upload of workspace files
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI has write_filesystem and subprocess execution, and next-ai-draw-io can also modify files and invoke MCP/API-backed tools. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared artifacts in the same workspace, so concurrent writes can clobber each other. Uncertainty about the exact shared-state setup pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or diagram file
IF the orchestrator does not serialize writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output paths
Run agents sequentially instead of concurrently
Enable file locking in the orchestrator
Snapshot inputs before each agent runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency checks

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI can generate outputs from tool-using agents, and next-ai-draw-io is explicitly AI-assisted visualization that can act on natural-language commands. If B treats A’s generated content as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can propagate into diagrams or downstream actions without verification. Because this can affect multiple work products by default, high is warranted.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io consumes CrewAI output as the source of truth
IF no verification or citation-check step is inserted before B renders or acts
mitigations: Require B to cite source documents
Insert a human verification gate
Limit A to draft-only outputs
Use schema validation on A’s outputs
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking before rendering

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles API keys and developer-passed crew data, while next-ai-draw-io processes documents and sends content to multiple external model providers. If regulated or sensitive documents are routed through B after A has touched them, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify a concrete jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared workflow
IF B forwards that data to a provider whose retention or residency terms differ from the source policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use only providers with approved DPAs
Disable logging of prompts and uploads
Document retention settings for both agents
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing by data class
